newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Rates seen keeping FTSE below 4000.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Rates seen keeping FTSE below 4000.

text.p: Britain's FTSE 100 index will not sustain its recent strength and will end the year below 4,000, according to an average of investment strategists' forecasts collected by Reuters on Monday.

Fears over potential interest rate hikes both in Britain and the U.S. should keep the FTSE at around 3,870 at the end of this year, but it would end 1997 at around 4,090, the average of forcasts from 12 strategists surveyed indicated.
Dealers said they believed the index, which hit a record 3,980.8 on Monday morning, was likely to break 4,000 some time this week, but some strategists were doubtful this pitch would be maintained.
"If we do get to 4,000 then profit-taking is almost inevitable," said Ian Williams, equity strategist at Panmure Gordon.
"It's riding for a fall," agreed Andrew Hartwill, UK equity strategist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.
Recent subdued U.S. inflation data cast doubt on the prospects for monetary tightening in the U.S., although strategists here said the markets were not out of the woods yet.
"We're anticipating a hike from the Fed whether this month or November and we're almost certainly at the bottom of the rate cycle here in the UK," Hartwill added.
Political uncertainty in Britain ahead of the general election which must be held before May 1997, could take the wind out of London stocks.
Opposition Labour is the current favourite to win in the opinion polls and is traditionally viewed as less market-friendly than the ruling Conservative party.

"A lot of the issues that the Labour party may bring on board have not been reflected in the market yet," said Allison Southey, global equity strategist at Nomura. Southey's forecasts, at 3,600 for both years, were the lowest of all strategists surveyed.
In addition, it is widely anticipated that the next government, whoever wins, will push up interest rates soon after coming to power.
But others were more optimistic about interest rate hikes. Robert Kerr, Nikko Europe's European equity strategist forecast a top-of-the-range 4,100 by the end of this year.

"The main factor is subdued long-term interest rates and reasonably good if not spectacular earnings forecasts," he said, adding that broad stable growth and low inflation would contribute to a good gilt market.
Improved conditions in other major markets would also shore up London stocks.

"As long as securities markets around the world are doing well, there's no reason to see the FTSE falling back. There's still a little upside," said David Aserkoff, vice president and equity strategist at CS First Boston.
